name: Copper Clad Laminates & PCB Base Materials
scope: The AI-server-driven global squeeze in CCL, glass cloth and copper foil, and India's first ECMS-backed laminate plants at Ratnaveer, Kaynes, Syrma and Amber (Wipro's plant is unlisted).

summary.one_line: New this edition: Ratnaveer's Q2 FY27 update says its CCL plant is 75% built. Machinery arrives by mid-November, slightly delayed, and trial runs start by 20 December. The company's own Phase-1 CCL case is far below broker spot-price maths, and we found no confirmation that order booking opened on 31 Oct. Syrma's Q2 revenue rose 73.6%, and its presentation now cites a 75:25 Shinhyup JV with commercial operations around March 2027. Citi expects another ~10% Kingboard hike in Nov-Dec.
key_points: Ratnaveer's CCL timeline has slipped by about a week. On 30-31 Oct it reported the plant about 75% complete. Machinery is now expected by mid-November, delayed by port connectivity and a shortage of shipping containers, and trial runs are to start by 20 Dec 2026 and last about a month (S22). In September, trial production was due in the second week of December (S4).

Ratnaveer's own CCL numbers are far smaller than the broker maths. Its Q2 presentation puts Phase 1 (one line, 15.84 lakh sheets a year) at Rs 108 cr revenue and Rs 22 cr EBITDA. The five-line FY31 case is Rs 750+ cr revenue and Rs 150 cr EBITDA (S23). Choice had estimated about Rs 600 cr from one line at ~Rs 5,500 per sheet, with Rs 750 cr CCL revenue by FY29 (S16). No CCL customers or binding orders were disclosed (S23).

Ratnaveer's core business carried the quarter. Q2 FY27 revenue was Rs 387.24 cr (+35.5% YoY), EBITDA margin 10.89% and PAT Rs 24.10 cr (+56.1%) (S22). The stock is at Rs 380 and 42.0x P/E, 2.6% below its 52-week high (S6), and about 44% above the Rs 264 rights price (S3).

Syrma's Q2 FY27 revenue was Rs 1,990 cr (+73.6%), EBITDA margin 9.7% and PAT Rs 117 cr (+83.1%). The Q2 material describes the Shinhyup PCB JV as 75:25 (Syrma 75%), against 51:49 in 2025 reports. It points to commercial operations around March 2027 at the Rs 800-900 cr Naidupeta plant (S24, S18). ICICI Direct had said April 2027 (S9).

The squeeze has not eased. Kingboard's eighth 2026 notice (13-14 Oct) raised laminate and prepreg on 2116-or-thinner cloth by 15% (S13, S25). Citi expects about a further 10% in Nov or Dec, though this is a forecast, not a notice. NextPCB reports new glass cloth capacity arriving mostly by end-2027 (S25). China Jushi's Q3 2026 net profit rose 173.8% YoY (S14).

India's dependence is unchanged. Ratnaveer puts CCL imports above 90% of a domestic market worth over Rs 5,000 cr (S5). IPCA says standard laminate lead times have stretched from about 4 weeks to as long as 20 (S21). ECMS offers a 25% capex incentive for laminate, copper foil and prepreg (S1), and cumulative approvals stand at Rs 69,548 cr (S12). We found no new tranche to 6 Nov.

Kaynes had not reported Q2 by 5 Nov; screener.in still shows June 2026 as the latest quarter (S7). It guides PCB commercialisation from Q3 FY27 (S11). Its ECMS approval covers CCL (S2), but no CCL date has been disclosed. The stock is at 64.7x P/E, 51.7% below its high (S7).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: Ratnaveer: its first line starts while laminate prices are still rising (S13, S25). Choice says the plant gets a 50% capex subsidy and buyers get a 2% cashback for buying locally (S16). The steel business grew Q2 PAT 56% while the plant is being built (S22).

Indian PCB makers would gain a local laminate source as import lead times stretch to as long as 20 weeks (S21). Ratnaveer's technology collaborator has committed to support customer approvals for 18-24 months after commissioning (S23).

Upstream suppliers could gain a local customer. Ratnaveer hopes to source copper foil from players like Hindalco and buys epoxy partly in India (S16). Atul makes epoxy for electrical and electronics uses (S10).

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: PCB and EMS makers that buy imported laminate. CCL inflation cut Amber's PCB margin to about 12% from a normal 16% (S15), and IPCA says some inputs cost 100-150% more (S21). Syrma's Q2 EBITDA margin slipped to 9.7% from 10.1% (S24).

Ratnaveer's equipment is already slightly late because of port and container problems (S22). Its glass fabric and copper foil will be imported at first (S16), and glass cloth is the input still rising fastest (S14, S25).

Ratnaveer has re-rated ahead of its first output. The stock is at Rs 380 versus the Rs 264 rights price (S6, S3), and the company's own Phase-1 CCL revenue case is only Rs 108 cr (S23). Promoter holding is 38.71% (S6). Syrma's PCB dates and JV terms have changed across disclosures (S9, S18, S24).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: Ratnaveer: machinery arrival by mid-November, trial runs from 20 Dec (S22), and any disclosure of customer orders, which have not yet been confirmed (S4, S23).
Kaynes: Q2 FY27 results and whether PCB commercialisation lands in Q3 FY27 (S7, S11). Syrma: equipment installation toward commercial operations around Mar-Apr 2027 (S24, S9).
Whether Kingboard issues the Nov-Dec hike Citi expects (S25), the glass cloth quotes (S14), and any new ECMS tranche (S12).

sections.title: What CCL is and why it is tight

subsections.title: CCL and prepreg in the PCB value chain

blocks.text: A copper clad laminate (CCL) is the base sheet of a PCB. It is woven electronic glass cloth impregnated with resin, usually epoxy, and clad with copper foil (S14). Prepreg is the resin-impregnated glass layer that bonds the layers of a multi-layer board (S2). PIB puts laminate at about 30% of a PCB's bill-of-materials cost (S19). NextPCB's example: a 20% laminate increase on a 30% laminate share adds roughly 6% to board cost (S25).

AI servers need low-loss laminates. Glass cloth makers are moving yarn, looms and staff toward low-Dk AI-server cloth, and that is what tightens supply of the standard cloth used in ordinary FR-4 (S14). Morgan Stanley expects a 31% shortfall of HVLP4 copper foil, used in high-end CCL, in 2027 (S17).

blocks.text: New supply takes time. Large new glass cloth capacity from Kingboard and International Composites is expected in 2027, and imported weaving equipment can take 18-24 months or more to arrive (S14). NextPCB reports no new cloth capacity at scale before end-2026, with most arriving by end-2027 (S25). Morgan Stanley sees the CCL market growing from US$19bn in 2025 to US$47bn by 2030 (S17).

The price data comes from trade press, vendor blogs and broker notes reported in the press, not an audited index. We could not open the Kingboard notices themselves, and the 15% October figure rests on one vendor blog (S13). The two 7628 quote series also differ (S14, S25).

sections.title: Import dependence, ECMS and Indian laminate capex

blocks.text: Ratnaveer puts India's CCL import share above 90% of a domestic market worth more than Rs 5,000 cr (company estimate, S5). IPCA says Indian PCB makers are struggling to secure laminates, resins, glass fibre and copper foil, and plans to seek duty concessions and working-capital support (S21).

blocks.caption: ECMS incentive structure for PCB and laminate segments

blocks.text: Source: India Briefing summary of ECMS guidelines (S1). With Gujarat's support, Ratnaveer is eligible for a 50% capex subsidy overall (S16). Cumulative ECMS approvals are Rs 69,548 cr after the 17 Aug tranche, which included a Rs 1,033 cr increase in Wipro's laminate project (S12). PIB's 30 Mar release lists laminate approvals for Syrma Components and Ratnaveer (S19). We found no new tranche between 17 Aug and 6 Nov.

blocks.text: For Syrma, the PCB project is still small relative to a group that reported Rs 1,990 cr of revenue in one quarter (S24). ICICI Direct models PCB contributing from FY28 at 15-17% EBITDA and about 1.5x asset turn (S9). Amber's PCB margin compression came from CCL inflation (S15), and Kingboard, Panasonic and Nan Ya have raised prices again since (S25).

subsections.title: Can Indian plants make AI-server grades?

blocks.text: No. Ratnaveer describes its project as FR-4 CCL (S22), and no Indian company has disclosed qualification for ultra-low-loss grades. Even China Jushi had no low-Dk revenue as of August 2026 (S14). Ratnaveer relies on a technical collaborator, with Chinese technical staff on 3-year contracts, and will import glass fabric and copper foil at first (S16, S23). Syrma relies on Korean partner Shinhyup (S18).

Our reading: the first Indian lines will make standard FR-4 for domestic consumer, auto and industrial PCBs, using imported glass fabric and copper foil (S16, S22). Ram Ratna Wires' 2023 plan for PCB laminates and copper foil has had no follow-up disclosure that we found (S20).

subsections.title: Broker coverage of the laminate angle

items: Choice Institutional Equities (6 Oct 2026, plant visit, not rated) calls Ratnaveer at an inflection point. Its monitorables are on-time Line 1 commissioning, PCB customer approvals and ramp-up working capital (S16).

ICICI Direct (27 Jul 2026) leaves CCL out of its FY27-28 Ratnaveer estimates until execution is clearer and puts the Rs 750+ cr CCL milestone in FY31 (S5). The company's Q2 presentation now also uses FY31 (S23).

ICICI Direct on Syrma (31 Jul 2026) models the PCB project contributing from FY28 on Rs 800-900 cr capex (S9). ICICI Direct on Amber (17 Aug 2026) quantifies the CCL cost hit at a ~12% PCB margin against a normal 16% (S15).
Global brokers, as reported: Citi expects another ~10% Kingboard hike in Nov-Dec (S25), and Morgan Stanley sees US$47bn of CCL by 2030 (S17).

Coverage that names the laminate angle for Indian stocks is still thin. Beyond Choice and ICICI Direct on Ratnaveer, we found mostly press-release reprints and results aggregators (S4, S22, S23), plus industry-body reporting (S21). We found no new broker note on the Q2 CCL update.

blocks.caption: Screener.in snapshot with reference points
rows: Rs 345 on 29 Oct (last edition); Rs 264 rights price; 1Y +109.4% to early Oct
Rs 1,563 on 29 Oct (last edition); P/E down from 75.0 after Q2 earnings

blocks.text: Sources: S6, S7, S8, S3, S16; 29 Oct prices from last edition's screener snapshot. Ratnaveer rose about 10% in the week of its Q2 update and is near its high, even though published broker estimates exclude CCL (S5). Syrma eased about 3% despite 73.6% revenue growth, with gross and EBITDA margins narrowing (S24). Kaynes is up about 6% but still far below its high, which ICICI Direct links to working capital, not laminates (S11).

items: Commissioning slippage. Ratnaveer has gone from 'commercial operations by November 2026' at approval (S5) to trial production in the second week of December (S4), and now to trial runs by 20 Dec, with machinery delayed by port and container issues (S22). Syrma moved from commissioning by Oct 2026 (S18) to commercial operations around Mar-Apr 2027 (S24, S9).

Imported inputs. Glass fabric and copper foil will be imported at first (S16), and glass cloth was still rising in October (S14, S25). Morgan Stanley expects HVLP4 foil to stay short through 2028 (S17).

Price cycle. New global cloth capacity arrives mostly by end-2027 (S25), when Indian lines will still be ramping up. The wide gap between the company and broker CCL revenue cases shows how sensitive the earnings are to price (S23, S16).

Customer qualification. Ratnaveer has disclosed no customers or binding orders (S23). Its collaborator's support for customer approvals runs 18-24 months after commissioning, which points to a long qualification phase (S23).
Funding and ownership. Ratnaveer raised Rs 329.99 cr in its rights issue (S3) and expects debt of Rs 475 cr by FY28E (S5). Promoter holding is 38.71% (S6).

companies.name: Ratnaveer Precision Engineering Ltd
companies.role: Stainless steel products maker building an ECMS- and Gujarat-backed FR-4 CCL plant in Vadodara. Phase 1 is one line of 15.84 lakh sheets a year, scalable to five lines (S22, S23, S16).
companies.impact: The plant is 75% complete, with trial runs by 20 Dec (S22). The company's own case is Rs 108 cr of Phase-1 CCL revenue and Rs 750+ cr by FY31 (S23), well below Choice's spot-price arithmetic (S16). Q2 PAT rose 56.1% on steel (S22). The stock is at 42.0x P/E, 2.6% off its high (S6).

companies.name: Kaynes Technology India Ltd
companies.role: EMS company whose subsidiary Kaynes Circuits holds an INR 32.8b ECMS approval for multi-layer and HDI PCBs, camera modules and CCL (S2).
companies.impact: PCB and OSAT commercialisation is guided from Q3 FY27, and no CCL date has been disclosed (S11). Q2 results were still pending as of 5 Nov. The stock is 51.7% below its 52-week high (S7).

companies.name: Syrma SGS Technology Ltd
companies.role: EMS company building a multi-layer PCB plant with Korea's Shinhyup at Naidupeta, AP. Its subsidiary Syrma Components holds an ECMS laminate approval (S24, S19, S18).
companies.impact: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 73.6% and PAT 83.1%, while EBITDA margin narrowed to 9.7% (S24). PCB commercial operations are due around Mar-Apr 2027, so laminate is immaterial to earnings before FY28 (S24, S9). The stock is at 63.5x P/E (S8).

companies.name: Amber Enterprises India Ltd
companies.role: AC and EMS maker investing about Rs 4,300 cr in bare PCBs under ECMS, with a first CCL plant planned by FY29-30 (S15).
companies.impact: CCL inflation cut its PCB margin to about 12% from 16% (S15), and laminate makers have raised prices again since (S25).

companies.name: Fine-Line Circuits Ltd
companies.role: Microcap PCB maker. Ratnaveer named 'Fine Line' among its target CCL customers (S16).
companies.impact: As a laminate buyer, it faces input inflation and long lead times (S21). It could benefit from local supply, but no order has been disclosed (S23).

companies.name: CG Power and Industrial Solutions Ltd
companies.role: Named by Ratnaveer management as a target CCL customer (S16).
companies.impact: Adjacent customer only. Laminate would be a small input, and no supply agreement has been disclosed (S23).

companies.name: Hindalco Industries Ltd
companies.role: Named by Ratnaveer as a prospective future domestic copper foil supplier for CCL (S16).
companies.impact: Adjacent large cap. We found no PCB-grade copper foil disclosure from Hindalco, so treat this as an option.

companies.name: Ram Ratna Wires Ltd
companies.role: Copper winding wire maker. Its board approved a Bhiwadi facility for PCBs, PCB laminates and copper foil in Mar 2023, at Rs 200 cr over five years (S20).
companies.impact: A stated laminate and copper-foil ambition with no further disclosure that we found. Treat it as an option, not a project.

companies.name: Atul Ltd
companies.role: Makes Lapox epoxy resins and curing agents for markets including electrical and electronics (S10).
companies.impact: Ratnaveer sources epoxy partly in India (S16), so Atul is a potential local resin supplier. It has disclosed no CCL-specific supply.

method: Weekly refresh of the 2026-W44 edition (30 Oct), researched on 6 Nov 2026 with web search and page fetches. Market data is screener.in as of 5 Nov 2026 (numbers.json). New this edition: Ratnaveer's Q2 FY27 results and CCL update (press release via Devdiscourse, with the BSE filing cross-checked via Arthneeti's announcement page) and a summary of its Q2 investor presentation (Multibagg.ai); Syrma's Q2 FY27 results and presentation summary (Multibagg.ai; the NSE press release PDF timed out); and NextPCB's table of 2026 Kingboard, Panasonic and Nan Ya notices plus Citi's Nov-Dec forecast. Searches found no confirmation that Ratnaveer's order booking opened on 31 Oct, no new ECMS tranche after 17 Aug, no new Kingboard notice after 13-14 Oct, and no Kaynes or Amber Q2 FY27 results as of writing. Sources carried over from last edition without re-opening this week: ECMS terms, broker notes (Choice, ICICI Direct), Jushi/glass cloth, Morgan Stanley/Citi via 36Kr, IPCA, PIB. Dropped as superseded or redundant: AtlasPCB (Q4 2026 forecast, replaced by NextPCB on capacity timing), the Goldman/UDN note, the Ind-Ra/Moneylife piece and the Arihant board-meeting page (meeting held). The Syrma JV ratio conflict (51:49 vs 75:25) is shown as reported, not resolved. Market-cap coverage: large cap (Hindalco, CG Power), mid cap (Kaynes, Syrma, Amber, Atul), small cap (Ratnaveer, Ram Ratna) and microcap (Fine-Line). Ratnaveer remains the only listed standalone laminate maker near commissioning, which reflects how early this niche is. No ratings or price targets.
